# E02 — Phase-4 type-aware eviction paired ablation

## Status

Proposed, opt-in internal evaluation. This package does not change product defaults, product locks, approval policy, or runtime behavior outside an explicitly launched ablation.

## Objective

Measure the effect of Phase-4 type-aware eviction against the leave-one-out Phase-4 FIFO baseline using the production `RuntimeMemoryStore`. The primary unit is a paired `(case, repetition)` observation. The baseline and treatment use the same deterministic seed and isolated store.

## Pre-registration

- Primary metric: `passAtK`, using the E01 definition and the fixture's `passAtK` thresholds.
- Also report: success, latency p50/p95, tokens proxy, false intercepts, safety violations, raw paired deltas, standardized effect, and a 95% confidence interval.
- Regression budgets are embedded in `shared/agent-dev/paired-ablation-fixture.json` before execution.
- A zero or negative treatment effect is a valid result. No winner selection, endpoint switching, or post-hoc budget relaxation is permitted.

## Corpus and controls

The local fixture contains 20 cases. Run three repetitions per case and condition with paired seeds. Insertions have a fixed per-case order. No provider or network call is permitted. Each condition must construct a fresh, isolated `RuntimeMemoryStore`.

Baseline: Phase-4 FIFO with type-aware eviction removed.  
Treatment: Phase-4 type-aware eviction enabled.

The harness rejects the run unless retained or evicted sets differ in at least one paired observation, proving that the component was observed and that the leave-one-out removal left no effective component trace.

## Required report

Include successful observations, pass^k, p50 and p95 latency, tokens proxy, false intercepts, safety violations, baseline and treatment distributions, paired mean/median effect, standardized effect, and a deterministic 95% interval. Report negative and zero effects unchanged.

## Acceptance

- Focused unit tests pass.
- Runtime/core type checks and scoped lint pass.
- Harness validation and dry-run pass.
- Credential scan has zero matches.
- `SHA256SUMS` is readable and verifiable.
- README translations are reviewed; because this is internal-only with no user-visible change, they remain unchanged.

## Reversibility

Disable the opt-in flag or stop running the harness to revert. No persisted setting, default, lock, or approval is changed.

# Paired ablation boundary

## Allowed

- Internal, explicitly invoked measurements using real `RuntimeMemoryStore` instances.
- Opt-in comparison of Phase-4 type-aware eviction with the same Phase-4 implementation after removing that component.
- Deterministic local fixtures, paired seeds, isolated stores, and statistical reporting.

## Forbidden

- Changing product defaults, product locks, approval settings, or user-visible runtime behavior.
- Provider calls, network access, credential access, or process side effects from fixture evaluation.
- Reading tests at runtime, weakening tests, changing graders, permissions, or dependency configuration.
- Selecting a winner after observing results, hiding zero/negative effects, changing preregistered metrics, or relaxing regression budgets.
- Treating a simulated map as the production `RuntimeMemoryStore`.

## Integrity requirements

The store factory, insert operation, retained-item inspection, and both eviction adapters must be supplied by the runtime caller. Every case/repetition pair must use the same seed across conditions and a fresh store for each condition. The run must fail if no retained/eviction set difference demonstrates that the treatment component was active.

Fixture data must contain at least 20 deterministic cases and three repetitions must be used by the task runner. Reports must include success, pass^k, latency p50/p95, tokens proxy, false intercepts, safety violations, effect sizes, and 95% intervals. Negative and zero effects are valid findings and require no corrective product change.

This rule governs internal evaluation only. It does not grant permission to bypass security checks, safety policies, locks, or approvals.

# E02 closure: paired Phase-4 eviction ablation

This document closes the evaluation design for an internal, opt-in paired ablation of Phase-4 type-aware eviction. It is not a product change.

## Method

The experiment compares two conditions on the production `RuntimeMemoryStore`:

1. **Baseline / leave-one-out:** Phase-4 FIFO with type-aware eviction removed.
2. **Treatment:** Phase-4 with type-aware eviction enabled.

Twenty deterministic local cases are executed three times in each condition. A case/repetition has one seed shared by both conditions. Stores are isolated and insertion order is fixed. There are no provider calls and no network dependency. A run fails when the retained and eviction sets are identical everywhere, because that would fail to demonstrate that the component was active.

The fixture preregisters `passAtK` as the primary metric and fixed regression budgets before execution. The report also contains success, p50/p95 latency, a deterministic tokens proxy, false intercepts, safety violations, paired deltas, standardized effect, and a 95% interval.

## Interpretation contract

Effects are reported as `treatment - baseline`. Negative latency/tokens/intercept/safety deltas and positive success/pass^k deltas favor treatment. The harness preserves the sign and explicitly labels zero and unfavorable effects. Confidence intervals may include zero; no significance claim is made solely from interval overlap.

A beneficial result establishes only an internal measurement. It does not justify changing a product default, product lock, approval rule, or release gate. A zero or negative result is also complete and requires no component removal unless a separate decision is recorded outside this evaluation.

## Reproducibility

The fixture is `shared/agent-dev/paired-ablation-fixture.json`; its canonical SHA-256 is included in each report. The library is `scripts/lib/paired-ablation.mjs`, with its public type contract in `scripts/lib/paired-ablation.d.mts`.

Verification consists of focused unit tests, runtime/core type checks, scoped lint, harness validate/dry-run, zero-match credential scan, and readable `SHA256SUMS`. README translations were reviewed: this package is internal-only and has no user-visible change, so the four README languages are not modified.
